rv.q: Mark Babych directs a pacy production, with Biddle's music linking the whole thing together perfectly.
This unsanctimonious entertainment carries a powerful moral message.
Oliver Twist at Hull Truck is far from a disappointment. It's a solid, respectable production with moments of real heart.
With carols bookending the production and a general goodwill feel, it once again proves that Dickens reigns supreme during the festive season.
It's funny, poignant, covers some quite harrowing subjects sensitively and deserves every accolade it will no doubt get.
The highest praise I can offer is that it takes the best of both, producing a truly memorable and thoroughly uplifting experience.

cn.t: McAndrew's bold adaptation delivers Dickens's darkness and light through a fresh musical lens, using carols and folk tunes to convey the stark contrast between rich and poor with broad humor and festive spirit.
